name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,190

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: UKIP throng’s bizarre collective mind-set

indicators.note: something bizarre is weirdly out of order, so the preceding words get scrambled

blocks.note: the party name and the crowd word supply all ten letters

explanation.surface: A crowd of UKIP supporters shares a strange, uniform way of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Groupthink is the conformist reasoning of a body of people who suppress dissent to agree.

clue.text: European holding a dry run for epic journey

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the nationality word wraps the rest

blocks.note: TT means teetotal, abstaining from drink
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A Greek athlete holding a trial run before some epic voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry for teetotal is a crossword staple; the nationality is split to wrap the middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Trek was the long nineteenth-century migration of Boer settlers into the South African interior.

clue.text: Nothing needed by Polish for Scottish lament

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
to hone is to sharpen or polish

explanation.surface: Polish people need nothing for a Scottish song of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Polish look like a nationality; it is the verb meaning to sharpen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohone is an old Scots and Irish exclamation of grief, a cry of mourning.

clue.text: Guards’ captain being paid to fight with a passion

blocks.note: a professional is paid to play
the article taken as written; with joins it on

explanation.surface: A professional soldier commanding guards fights with zeal because he is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A protospataire was a Byzantine court official, commander of the imperial guard of sword-bearers.

clue.text: Hot sauce includes about 50 per cent rice with it

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word means just two of its letters are kept
a word that includes something holds it within, and about reinforces the surrounding

blocks.note: the first half of the grain
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A chilli sauce whose recipe is half rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword favourite; 'Hot' looks like wordplay for H but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a fiery North African chilli paste used as a condiment.

clue.text: Oath men devised never again used by poet

indicators.note: something devised is invented and arranged anew, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Men who swore an oath vowed a poet would never be heard again.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Spenser, who used this archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathemo is a Spenserian adverb meaning never more, recorded in Chambers as poetic.

clue.text: An opening in Edinburgh or Belfast: small capitals you used in the past

definitions.text: An opening in Edinburgh or Belfast

blocks.note: SC is the printer's abbreviation for small capitals
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A tourist guide notes small capital cities once used by visitors to Scotland and Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh and Belfast point to Scotland and Northern Ireland, where the word is used; capitals is printing, not cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A scye is the armhole of a garment, a dialect word in Scotland and Ulster.

clue.text: Energy wasted covering shields for light reflector

indicators.note: to shield something is to cover it on every side, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: a coat is a covering layer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy is wasted covering shields that reflect light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' reads as the container signal, but it is the outer word; 'shields' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A coelostat is a rotating mirror that reflects sunlight or starlight steadily into a fixed telescope.

clue.text: Look to bring about trial of revolutionary antibacterial liquid

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the preceding letters run the other way

blocks.note: to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries face trial over a germ-killing fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eusol is an Edinburgh University solution of hypochlorite used as an antiseptic wound dressing.

clue.text: Green package, perhaps, church returned: books belonging to us

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A green holiday package returned to the church with our books.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecotour is an environmentally friendly holiday, sold as a green package deal.

clue.text: Local insists on what apprenticeship has, perhaps just missing out

blocks.note: the word apprenticeship contains this many of one letter
the letter in question, as a plural; the tail hedges the count

explanation.surface: A local insists on what an apprenticeship provides, perhaps narrowly missing out.
explanation.walkthrough: Apprenticeship is spelt with three Ps; the closing words are the setter's hedge on that tally, with no letters of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Threep is a Scots verb meaning to insist or maintain obstinately, so a dialect speaker threeps.

clue.text: Ultimately, their murmur goes on spreading?

definitions.text: Ultimately, their murmur goes on spreading?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used
spreading scatters things about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: In the end, gossips' whispers keep on spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: what such people do is let their murmur go on spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumourmongers are people who spread gossip, and the clue describes their murmurs travelling outward.

clue.text: Old club backed exercise system

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: An old club backed a fitness regime.
explanation.walkthrough: Club looks like a society or golf club; it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Tae-Bo is an aerobic workout combining martial-arts kicks and punches with dance moves.

clue.text: Good engine fuel succeeded — a lot came free

indicators.note: letters set free can fall into any order

explanation.surface: Fuel for a locomotive came free in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam coal is coal suited to raising steam in boilers, as for railway engines.

clue.text: Brazilian ready to collect drinks before our crossing desert: that speaks for itself

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one word takes another inside it
to cross something is to go over it, so the possessive straddles the next word

blocks.note: ready is slang for cash, and the real is Brazil's currency

explanation.surface: A Brazilian ready for drinks before crossing the desert says it all.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(SIPS)AL then O(QUIT)UR. Ready is British slang for money; desert is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Res ipsa loquitur is the Latin legal maxim meaning the thing speaks for itself, used where negligence is obvious.

clue.text: Being fed up, returning sons post letters from abroad

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the whole string is read from the end

explanation.surface: Sons returning home post letters from abroad, tired of it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Satedness is the state of being satisfied to excess, which is what being fed up literally means.

clue.text: Rival in speed contest for third time, maybe assuming black piece of armour

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on board, so it goes inside

blocks.clueFragment: Rival in speed contest for third time, maybe
blocks.note: to race again a second time, a re-re-race

explanation.surface: A competitor racing for a third time dons black armour.
explanation.walkthrough: Racing a third time is racing again again, written with a doubled RE prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerebrace is plate armour for the upper arm, worn above the elbow.

clue.text: Girl briefly visiting her doctor satisfied about backing measure to detect onset of cold

definitions.text: measure to detect onset of cold

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the name loses its last letter
backing goes in reverse, so the short word runs the other way

blocks.note: visiting somewhere, you are at it

explanation.surface: A girl visiting her doctor is satisfied the measurement can spot a coming cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sniffle; the cold is the cooling power of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A katathermometer is an alcohol thermometer measuring the cooling power of the air by timing its fall in temperature.

clue.text: Tax from copper and silver brought in about four o’clock?

indicators.note: things brought in are taken inside, so the metals sit within the direction

blocks.note: on a compass laid over a clock face, four o'clock points roughly east-south-east
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A tax levied in copper and silver coins, collected around teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Four o'clock suggests tea; read the clock as a compass, where three o'clock is east.
explanation.definitionFit: Escuage, or scutage, was a feudal payment made in lieu of a knight's military service.

clue.text: Business graduate encountering curse in African city

blocks.note: a bane is a curse or affliction

explanation.surface: A business graduate meets a curse while working in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mbabane is the administrative capital of Eswatini, formerly Swaziland.

clue.text: One avenging spirit: lawyer penning letter

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: the ka is the soul in Egyptian belief
the spelt-out name of a letter

explanation.surface: A vengeful spirit: a lawyer writing a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avenging spirit' looks like the definition, but spirit belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A kadaitcha is an Aboriginal Australian man who exacts ritual vengeance on an offender.

clue.text: Pudding upset this country lass of good breeding

indicators.note: in a down entry an upset turns things upside down, so the letters run upward

blocks.note: gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: A well-bred young woman upset by a national dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Kugel is a baked Jewish pudding of noodles or potato.

clue.text: Producer of oil fine embrocation contains

indicators.note: the phrase contains the answer within its run of letters

blocks.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A source of oil is in a fine liniment.
explanation.definitionFit: The neem tree's seeds yield neem oil, used in medicine and pesticides.

clue.text: Burns created these ashes? Around fifty become less severe

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Did burning make these ashes, or will the fire die down?
explanation.walkthrough: Burns is Robert Burns, the Scottish poet who used the word; the question mark flags the pun on burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Easle is a Scots word for hot embers or cinders, found in Burns's poetry.

clue.text: Primate finally putting virtu before zeal, oddly

indicators.note: finally points to the ends of words, so the closing letters are kept
oddly keeps the odd-numbered positions of a word

blocks.note: the closing letter of each word
ere is the old word for before

explanation.surface: A primate finally prefers artistic taste to zeal, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: The guereza is a black-and-white colobus monkey of East Africa.

clue.text: Failure to digest and copy extra comment, one with answer

explanation.surface: An indigestion sufferer copies an extra note, one with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apepsia is the medical term for absence or failure of digestion.

clue.text: How male comes to make regional side

blocks.note: surface: a question of how a man comes to make something
setter's reading: a dialect word for the flank or groin, the body region a man's procreation starts from

explanation.surface: Wondering how a man comes to create a local team.
explanation.walkthrough: Regional side sounds like a county team; it is a dialect word for part of the body, with the opening words a racy hint at its role.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisk is a northern English dialect word for the groin or flank, the side of the body below the ribs.

clue.text: Wine taken from safe appeared unfinished

indicators.note: something unfinished stops short, so the verb loses its closing letter

blocks.note: peter is underworld slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Wine was apparently taken from the safe in a job left half done.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old criminal slang for a safe, the kind a safe-cracker blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter-see-me is an old name for a Spanish wine made from the Pedro Ximénez grape.
